6 25-02-2026 Heard Mr. Sunil Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Rajni Kant Pandey, learned counsel representing the informant beside Mrs. Asha Kumari, learned APP.

2. The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 606(C) of 2022 for the offence under sections 498A of the Indian Penal Code and section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act lodged by the informant, Kanchan Kumari Verma.
3. As per the complaint, the lady alleged that the marriage took place in the year 2019 but she was always Patna High Court CR.

MISC. No.25582 of 2025(6) dt.25-02-2026 tortured for SUV car and in continuation of that, she was regularly thrashed which followed the Complaint Case No. 678 of 2020 but as they compromised, the same was closed.
Later, they again resorted to torture and assault which led to the present complaint case.

sentences.text:
In the present case, the Court wanted the couple to come to an amicable settlement as the petitioner is holding the post of Branch Manager in the Bank of Baroda, Head Office, Baroda,
Gujrat.
5. Pursuant to the earlier orders, the petitioner as also the complaint are present.
This Court gave them some time to come to terms but it seems that, for the present, they are not ready to reconcile.

However, this Court appreciates the stand of the petitioner that he on his own submitted that presently he is paying Rs. 12,000/- to the lady but now wants to enhance it to Rs. 15,000/- per month which he shall be paying by 10th of every month beginning from March 2026.

6. As recorded above, for the present, they are not ready to continue their marital journey, expecting that they will come to terms/reunite in future, taking into account the aforesaid facts as also that the petitioner has no criminal antecedent, is holding a post, sending him to jail will not serve Patna High Court CR.

MISC. No.25582 of 2025(6) dt.25-02-2026 any purpose and is ready to pay Rs.
15,000/- per month by 10 th of every month beginning March 2026, in that background, this Court is inclined to extend him the privilege of anticipatory bail with conditions.
